xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Office Of the Assistant Commissioner, Central Goods & Services Tax, Division-IV, E-5, SECTOR-1, NOIDA-201301
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak:
Company received Demand notice dated October 17, 2025 from the Assistant Commissioner, CGST, Division IV, Noida, under Section 74 of the CGST Act, 2017, for FY 2018-19 and 2019-20, alleging non-payment of IGST on OIDAR services provided by Facebook Ireland Ltd. to non-taxable recipients in India. Demand was raised for interest amounting to Rs. 3,291/- along with penalty of Rs. 1,281/-.
Amount for the interest of Rs 3,291 and penalty of Rs 1,281 were paid on October 28, 2025 by the Company.
Tax authorities acknowledged the payment and issued an order in Form GST DRC-07 dated October 30, 2025, dropping the proceedings.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: Notice in form GST DRC-01 issued under Section 74 of the CGST Act 2017 for alleging non-payment of IGST
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: The matter stands concluded. and the Company does not expect any material financial impact arising therefrom
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Office of the Joint Commissioner (ST), Intelligence-I, Chennai - 600006
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak:
Company received Penalty notice under Section 129 of the CGST Act, 2017, in Form GST MOV-07 from the State Tax Officer, Roving Squad IV, Chennai, on November 12, 2025, in relation to detention of goods during transit amounting to Rs. 4,55,550/-. The goods were transported with a valid tax invoice and e-way bill but were detained as the “ship-to” address was not reflected in the customer’s GST registration records. The Company submitted its explanation that the customer had an active GST registration and had applied for amendment to add the additional place of business.
To secure release of the goods, the Company deposited penalty of Rs 2,27,775/- under CGST and Rs 2,27,775/- SGST under protest through Form DRC-03 dated November 18, 2025.
The Company believes that it has a strong case on merits against the demand order received and an appeal has been filed on January 02, 2026 before the appropriate appellate authority against the said order.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: Notice in form GST MOV-07 under section 129 of CGST Act, 2017 for wrong declaration of shipping address on the invoice.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: The Company does not expect any material adverse financial impact arising out of the aforesaid matter.

Company received a scrutiny notice in Form GST ASMT-10, followed by a Show Cause Notice dated September 24, 2025, under Section 73 of the CGST Act, 2017, for FY 2021–22, alleging excess availment of ITC in GSTR-3B as compared to GSTR-2A amounting to Rs. 3,841/- under CGST and Rs. 3,841/- under SGST
The Company deposited excess ITC availed during Q2 2025-26, Subsequently department issued the order with addition of interest of Rs 6,388 and penalty of Rs 10,000 under CGST and Rs 10,000 under SGST on December 22, 2025. Company paid the interest and penalty amount and matter has been concluded by the GST authorities.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: Order issued in form GST DRC-07 under section 73 of CGST Act, 2017 for a demand alleging excess availment of ITC
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: The matter stands concluded. and the Company does not expect any material financial impact arising therefrom
